trajectory_summary: This call moves efficiently and without friction: the customer is cooperative from the start, the bill is captured almost instantly, and a specific day/time is locked in phone-appointment format. The rep's handling of a real calendar/password failure at 06:05 is a positive transparency moment, but the unresolved co-owner status is left ambiguous and then quietly resolved in the rep's favor rather than the customer's clarity.

observed_outcome.quote: K. Great. Well, I'll get you solidified, for Thursday at ten, and then I'll send you a text just with your appointment details so you can add it to your calendar as well.
observed_outcome.reasoning: A specific day and time (Thursday at 10) are agreed and confirmed by the customer, and the rep commits to a text follow-up, meeting the bar for booked; however, the wife's title/co-owner status was never confirmed, so co_owner_confirmed is false despite the booking proceeding.

primary_coaching_focus.topic: unresolved co-owner status booked as single-attendee
primary_coaching_focus.quote: I guess if your wife isn't on the title, then we could just do it with you.
primary_coaching_focus.why: The customer never confirmed his wife's title status ('I'd have to look at that') and the rep converts that uncertainty into a reason to book Jim alone rather than closing the loop — this is the single biggest structural risk to the appointment holding, since a real co-decision-maker may be excluded from the closer call.

key_moments.quote: No. I mean, maybe my wife. I'm not I'd have to look at that, but it it the two of us, we live together, still married.
key_moments.stewart_read: The customer explicitly says he doesn't know if his wife is on the title. The rep accepts 'no problem' and never circles back to confirm before the appointment is booked, leaving a live co-decision-maker's involvement undetermined at close.

key_moments.quote: Mhmm. Yeah. No problem. So, yeah, I can try I can give you some information. I don't know, like, as much as a specialist, of course, just because I'm a scheduler.
key_moments.stewart_read: Rep proactively self-labels as 'a scheduler' and caveats his own program explanation before delivering it — this is a boundary-setting move, not scope creep, since the immediately following content (credit threshold, savings guarantee, state incentives) tracks the qualifiers.credit_qualifier script almost verbatim.

key_moments.quote: Yeah. Okay. Alright. Yeah. That's good to know. We can definitely help get that cut down. I know that ComEd is they've been raising their rates quite a bit from what I've heard, so I'm glad you guys are looking into an an alternative.
key_moments.stewart_read: This is the closest the rep gets to a flip — he references ComEd's rising rates and frames solar as 'an alternative' right after the customer states a $150-$270 monthly range. It's directionally aligned with objection_inversion (aligning against the utility) but stays generic ('they've been raising rates from what I've heard') rather than tying the specific dollar figure back to the customer as personal leverage.

key_moments.quote: And then, yeah, your home looks pretty good for solar. The roof looks good and everything.
key_moments.stewart_read: The rep asserts a visual roof assessment ('the roof looks good') before asking any roof detail question, which is an authority claim not grounded in anything stated on the call at that point.
